title: Wyoming Statutes, Title 40 - Trade and Commerce, Chapter 12 - Consumer Protection, Article 1 - In General
source_id: Wyo. Stat. Ann. tit. 40, ch. 12, art. 1 (ss 40-12-101 through 40-12-114)
verified_how: walked the LSO NXT table of contents (gateway.dll?f=xmlcontents&command=getchildren) down to 'TITLE 40 - TRADE AND COMMERCE' > 'CHAPTER 12 - CONSUMER PROTECTION' > 'ARTICLE 1 - IN GENERAL', running from '40-12-101. Short title.' to '40-12-114. Effect on other remedies.'. Repealed sections are shown in the same listing with a 'Repealed by Laws ...' catchline (e.g. '37-3-103. Repealed by Laws 1995, ch. 192, s 3.'), so the substantive catchlines above are live text. Currency: the LSO's Statutes Download page states 'This version of the Wyoming Statutes contains changes from the 2026 Budget Session and reflects the contents of the statutes as they exist as of July 1, 2026'; the NXT infobase I browsed is the one labelled '2026 Wyoming Statutes' (the register also keeps 2020-2025 as separate historical infobases). Official title PDF at https://wyoleg.gov/statutes/compress/title40.pdf.
notes: This is the Wyoming Consumer Protection Act (deceptive trade practices, Attorney General enforcement, private remedies). THE TENANCY HALF OF THIS TOPIC IS A DIFFERENT STATUTE and a human should decide whether to encode it too: residential tenancies sit in Title 1, Chapter 21, Article 12 - Residential Rental Property, ss 1-21-1201 ('Definitions.') through 1-21-1211 ('Owner's remedies; eviction; judicial remedies; damages.'), verified on the register in the same session, with eviction procedure in the adjacent art. 10 Forcible Entry and Detainer and art. 14 Removal of Unauthorized Occupants. Wyoming has no uniform residential landlord and tenant act; art. 12 is short (11 sections) but it is the whole of the state's residential tenancy statute. Consumer credit is separately in Title 40, ch. 14 (Wyoming Uniform Consumer Credit Code).
